h1: Using WhatsApp broadcasts and groups to fill a brewpub midweek
title: WhatsApp Marketing for Brewpubs | Craft Beer School
desc: How a brewpub can use WhatsApp broadcasts, groups and channels to fill quiet midweek nights, with opt-in, frequency and alcohol rules covered.
teaser: Most Indian brewpub regulars check WhatsApp more often than Instagram. Used well, one message on a Tuesday can fill a Wednesday.
standfirst: Midweek nights are where many brewpubs lose money. WhatsApp is already on every regular's phone, but used badly it gets you muted or blocked. Here is how to use broadcasts, groups and channels to bring people in on quiet nights.
sections:
In India, WhatsApp is the app people actually open. Messages get read in minutes, not days. For a brewpub, that makes it a direct line to regulars, without paying a platform to show your post to your own followers.

It suits midweek problems in particular. A Friday fills itself. A Tuesday needs a reason: a new beer, a quiz, a food pairing night, a live acoustic set. WhatsApp lets you tell the people most likely to come, at the right moment.

Broadcast lists in the WhatsApp Business app send one message to many contacts, each receiving it privately. Only people who have saved your number receive broadcasts, which acts as a natural opt-in. Each list has a size limit, so larger audiences need several lists or the Business Platform.

Groups let regulars talk to each other. They suit a small, engaged community, such as a beer club or tasting group, but need moderation and can get noisy.

Channels are one-way updates people choose to follow. They work for general announcements without exposing members' numbers.

Larger brewpubs sometimes use the WhatsApp Business Platform through a provider, with approved message templates and per-message charges. Start with the free app and move up only when you outgrow it.

Only message people who have asked to hear from you. Good ways to build the list:

  • A QR code on tables and the bill folder: "Get our new beer alerts on WhatsApp."
  • Staff mentioning it to regulars who enjoy a night.
  • A sign-up at events and tastings.

Never add numbers from bills or bookings without permission. People report unwanted messages, which can get your number restricted. India's data protection law also expects consent and care with personal data. Make opting out easy: "Reply STOP and we will remove you."
What to send and how often

Once a week is plenty for most brewpubs. More than that and people mute you. Good midweek messages:

  • New beer on tap. A photo, two lines on taste and when it is pouring.
  • Event reminders. "Quiz night tomorrow, 8 pm. Teams of up to six. Reply to book a table."
  • Food pairings. "This week the kitchen is pairing our stout with mutton sukka."
  • Brewer moments. A short video from brew day.

Keep messages short, with one clear action. Send them a day or two ahead, in the late afternoon when people plan their evenings.

WhatsApp's commerce policy does not allow selling alcohol through its catalogue or payment features, so invite people to the brewpub rather than trying to sell beer in the chat. Keep within Indian alcohol advertising rules: no heavy drinking messages, no offers that push quantity and no messages to anyone under the legal drinking age.

A small group of regulars can become the heart of your community. Name an admin, set simple rules and post useful things: tasting notes, brewery news, first chance to try a pilot batch. Let members talk. A group where only the brewpub posts is just a broadcast with extra noise.

Our guide to building a beer community covers how groups like this grow into loyal regulars.

Track whether messages fill seats. Simple methods:

  • Ask guests to mention the message for a table booking.
  • Compare covers on nights with a message against similar nights without.
  • Count replies and bookings from each message.

After a month, you will see which messages bring people in. New beer alerts and quiz nights often work better than general "come visit us" messages. Use what works with your taproom events calendar.
Making it part of a bigger plan

WhatsApp works best alongside reviews, social media and search, each feeding the others. A guest finds you on Google, enjoys a night, joins your WhatsApp list and comes back for quiz night. Building that chain on purpose is what turns a quiet Tuesday into a habit for your regulars.

Start small this week. Put a QR code on every table, write four short messages for the next month and pick one quiet night to test them on. Count the covers before and after. The numbers will tell you more than any marketing theory.
faqs: How often should a brewpub send WhatsApp broadcasts?
About once a week is enough for most. More often and people tend to mute or block the number.
Can we add customers' numbers from bills to our WhatsApp list?
No. Only message people who have opted in. Make it easy to opt out. Unwanted messages can get your number restricted.
Can a brewpub sell beer through WhatsApp?
WhatsApp's commerce policy does not allow selling alcohol through its catalogue or payments. Use it to invite people to the brewpub instead.
